Anita — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Looping in Rishi (inference/ops) and Jonas (solutions) to capture the sizing and procurement notes.

High level answers up front:
- Private (customer-managed VPC or on‑prem) gives you the strongest control for PHI (KMS/HSM integration, tenant network isolation, long retention logs). Lead time for an on‑prem package is typically 8–12 weeks (hardware procurement + validation); VPC-based Private (our managed image into your AWS account) is ~3–6 weeks depending on network approvals.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our hosted infra) is available in 2–4 weeks and supports strict isolation across tenant namespaces, but the control plane remains hosted — good for faster time to value if your compliance team accepts that model.
- For your 50k monthly convo tokens estimate we'll attach a quick sizing table; decision levers are peak concurrency and request latency SLOs (50ms vs 200ms per token).

A couple quick Qs to make the sizing tighter:
1) Expected peak concurrent sessions during business hours?
2) Typical average sequence length per session (prompt + response) — an average token per call estimate helps pick the batching profile.
3) Are there hard constraints on model family? (e.g., must we run a privacy‑validated LLM variant or are open model options acceptable?)

I'll drop a short one‑pager and a spreadsheet (isolation_sizing_table.xlsx) in the next message.

Anita — adding the technical estimates below based on the 50k monthly convo tokens baseline and a conservative peak concurrency assumption (see attached sizing sheet for math):

Summary (Pilot — 6 months)
- Workload: 50k conv tokens / month ≈ ~1.7k tokens/day (assume 20 business days)
- Baseline model: 7B/13B family quantized (production-verified by Redwood) to balance latency and cost
- Pilot concurrency target: 4 concurrent sessions (burst to 8)
- Recommended committed capacity (Dedicated): 1 x A100-80GB equivalent node with continuous batching and prefix caching. This supports ~80–120 rps token throughput depending on sequence length and batching; allows low latency (50–120ms/token) for short sessions.
- Recommended Private (VPC/on‑prem): 1 x A100 or 2 x A40s (if you prefer smaller instances for on‑prem procurement) — add a hot standby node for HA if SLAs require 99.95% availability.

Summary (Production — 12 month, full rollout)
- Baseline growth assumptions: 3–4x usage uplift after productization (150–200k conv tokens/mo)
- Dedicated: reserve 2–3 x A100 nodes (or equivalent) for predictable throughput; autoscale burst pool for peak spikes.
- Private: 3 x A100 with 1 hot standby (N+1) or 6 x A40s for a tiled setup to reduce single-card procurement risk.

Tradeoffs (short):
- Compliance: Private > Dedicated (from customer control perspective). Private supports full log retention in your KMS and network boundaries; Dedicated can provide tenant isolation and per‑route audit logs but the control plane is hosted.
- Cost: Dedicated (hosted) generally has lower upfront capital and faster onboarding. Private requires hardware procurement and higher initial TCO but offers long‑term unit cost control and clear boundary for PHI.
- Lead time: Dedicated (2–4w) << Private on‑prem (8–12w). VPC-based Private sits in the middle.

Attachment notes: isolation_sizing_table.xlsx includes conservative/conservative+growth scenarios, expected token throughput per GPU at 4/8/16 concurrency, and a short ops checklist for Private installs (network CIDR, egress rules, HSM/KMS endpoint, audit log sink).

Jonas — I added a config stub (redwood-dedicated-config.yaml) we can use in the proposal for deployment automation. Laura — looping you for procurement language (SLA/credits for migration).
